description: Ground truth for scripts/validate_ucl.py. Every value below was measured empirically on 2026-09-29 by running Elias 1.x inside wuxia_mud_dev-app-1 against the fixtures in this directory, plus the corrected check semantics (NOT the current buggy .exs).

checker.token_note: The keys under "checks" and the entries in "check_order" are lowercase logical ids. The "failing_checks" arrays below use the exact capitalised tokens that the tool prints on stdout, e.g. `❌ Syntax: ...`.

exit_codes.1: at least one check failed (also used for unreadable file)
exit_codes.2: wrong argument count; usage printed to stderr

checker.stdout_on_success: ✅ All checks passed: <path exactly as passed on the command line>
checker.stdout_on_failure: one line per failing check, in check_order, formatted as `❌ <Check>: <detail>` with <Check> = Encoding|Syntax|Structure|Integrity|Chars
invariants: All 5 checks always run. A failure never short-circuits the remaining checks.
The tool must never raise an uncaught exception or print a traceback, for ANY input (including invalid UTF-8 and truncated files).
The failing check NAMES and the exit code are normative. The free-text <detail> is not, except that Syntax details must include a 1-based line number.
Over-reporting and under-reporting are both failures: the failing set must match exactly.

rules: bytes must decode as UTF-8
must NOT start with EF BB BF (UTF-8 BOM)
must NOT start with FF FE (UTF-16LE BOM)
must NOT contain any 0x0D byte (LF-only)

syntax.input: UTF-8 decoded text (decode failures are reported as an encoding failure and also make syntax fail)
rules: A hand-written minimal UCL recursive-descent parser covering the syntax subset that scripts/lpc_converter.py actually emits.

Must support: top-level `name "v" { ... }` and `name { ... }` blocks; block members `key = value`; nested inline objects `key = { ... }` (recursive); arrays `[ ... ]` (possibly empty, multi-line, elements may be `{ k = v }`); scalars = double-quoted string (with \" escapes), number, bare identifier including dotted references like rooms.damen.id, `[]`, `{}`.
Comments: `#` to end of line. A closing brace may be glued to the end of a value, e.g. `north = rooms.a.id  }`.
Must ACCEPT every `*_ok_*` fixture, and must REJECT 10, 11, 12, 40, 42 and 52.
these three patterns must each be found somewhere in the file (multiline search): ^\s*zones\s+"\w+" ; ^\s*rooms\s+"\w+" ; ^\s*room_exits\s+"\w+"
the detail must list which ones are missing
rooms_count = number of matches of ^\s*rooms\s+"(\w+)"
room_exits_count = number of matches of ^\s*room_exits\s+"(\w+)"
PASS requires rooms_count == room_exits_count AND rooms_count > 0
detail is `rooms(N) != room_exits(M)` or `no rooms defined`
NOTE: use [ \t] (horizontal whitespace) here, NOT \s.
^[ \t]*}[ \t]*}  ->  double closing brace `} }`
,[ \t]*}          ->  trailing comma before `}`
an odd total number of `"` bytes in the file  ->  unpaired double quote
raw `$N` or `$n` placeholders not replaced by converter (must be {npc}/{name})
square brackets inside string literals (elias parser rejects them; converter should emit ( ) )
duplicate direction keys inside a single `room_exits "..."` block (elias merges them into an array, so the loader's String.split receives an array and crashes)

raw Python repr leaking into a UCL value, i.e. a single-quoted token directly after `[` or `{`, or a `'key': 'value'` pair. UCL only ever writes `key = value` with double quotes, so this can only come from the converter interpolating str(dict)/str(list). The detail must include the 1-based line number.

an unconverted LPC runtime expression leaking into an object id, i.e. an `items.`/`characters.`/`rooms.` reference whose local name contains a subscript `[...]`, a `$var` interpolation, or parentheses (e.g. `items. + books[random(sizeof(books))].id`). The converter must skip such keys rather than emit them. The detail must include the 1-based line number.

cases.why: minimal well-formed zone: 1 room, 1 room_exits

valid, and it reproduces a real lpc_converter layout where item_desc's ` }` is immediately followed by the rooms block's `    }` on consecutive lines. The current .exs check_chars FALSE-POSITIVES on this; the Python MUST let it pass.
valid; comments contain an even number of double quotes, so the quote-parity rule must not fire
unclosed `{`

regression fixture for the real lpc_converter bug: `direction = ""north""`. Also has consecutive `}`-only lines, so the current .exs check_chars false-positives here too; only `syntax` may be reported.
unterminated string literal in `name = "odd'`
no `zones "..."` block
no `room_exits "..."` block, so rooms(1) != room_exits(0)
only a zones block; pins the `rooms > 0` branch of the integrity rule (0 == 0 must still fail)
2 rooms vs 1 room_exits
a genuine stray `} }` on one line, which is both a syntax error and a chars violation

regression fixture for the real shaolin bug: room_exits "zhonglou6" got two `up` keys (one from the LPC source, one added by assign_room_coords.py's vertical-link pass). elias merges duplicate keys into an array, so the loader crashed with String.split(["rooms.bagua1.id", "rooms.zhonglou7.id"], ".", []). Note the duplicate direction is still syntactically valid, so only `chars` may be reported.

regression fixture for the real taishan bug: _parse_accept_body() computed `has_specific_rules = money_rule is not None or item_id_rules or item_name_rules`, which returns the non-empty LIST `item_name_rules` rather than a bool, and _build_accept_ucl() then interpolated str(list) straight into the output. Two independent checks must catch this: syntax (the `'key': 'value'` pair has no `=`) and chars (the python-repr rule).

regression fixture for the real wudang bug: cangjingge.c declares `string* books = ({...})` and spawns `"/clone/book/" + books[random(sizeof(books))]`. The key is a *string* containing "/", so the converter's _looks_like_path accepted it and _room_id_from_path returned the basename `books[random(sizeof(books))]`, emitting `items. + books[random(sizeof(books))].id` straight into the UCL. Only `syntax` is reported: the subscript breaks the dotted-reference grammar, and a chars-side rule was deliberately NOT added because shaolin legitimately contains `items.fojing1+random(2).id` (from `"d/shaolin/obj/fojing1"+random(2)`), so no chars rule can tell the two apart without false positives.

regression fixture for the real xiangyang bug, found by the container rather than by any static check: wuxiuwen.c maps each item name to an LPC closure `(: ask_me_1, "weibo" :)`. elias 0.2.8 lexes with a Word pattern that does NOT exclude the comma, so leex's longest match normally swallows "a," into one word token; the digit in `ask_me_1` terminates the word, the comma then lexes as its own `comma` token, and elias_parser.yrl has no `words -> comma ...` production. Elias.parse/1 therefore aborts with `syntax error before: ', ['"']` and the whole world fails to boot (Kantele.World.Kickoff terminating). Measured: "(: a, 'b' :)" and "(: a_b, 'c' :)" parse; "(: a1, 'b' :)" and "(: ask_me_1, 'b' :)" do not. The syntax check cannot see this (the file is well-formed UCL), so `chars` is the only check that fires.
CRLF line endings. Measured: Elias parses it SUCCESSFULLY, so only `encoding` may be reported.
UTF-8 BOM. The current .exs check_encoding MISSES this (it only tests FF FE); the Python MUST reject it. Measured: Elias parses the BOM file successfully, so only `encoding` may be reported.
trailing comment contains raw FF FE bytes. Must produce a clean verdict, not a traceback. Measured: Elias raises `invalid encoding starting at <<255, 254, 10>>`.

real_world_regression.description: Verified end-to-end on 2026-09-29. Note that the pre-coords file is EXPECTED to fail: that failure is the point of the coords step, not a regression.

cases.why: full converter output for the test zone, coordinates already present. Contains raw $N/$n placeholders from legacy converter (should be {npc}/{name}).

PRE-coords converter output. rooms(34) != room_exits(33): room `liandan_lin` is an orphan with no `room_exits` block at all. assign_room_coords.py synthesises the missing block for orphan rooms, so this file is legitimately 'unfinished' and the validator is right to reject it. This is the evidence that the SOP order (validate -> assign coords -> validate) is meaningful. Also contains raw $N/$n placeholders from legacy converter.
the same file after assign_room_coords.py; rooms(34) == room_exits(34), all rooms covered. Contains raw $N/$n placeholders from legacy converter (should be {npc}/{name}).

known_exs_defects_do_not_reproduce.defect: check_syntax/1 matches {:ok, _} / {:error, err}, but Elias.parse/1 returns a BARE MAP on success and RAISES on failure.
known_exs_defects_do_not_reproduce.measured: running scripts/validate_ucl.exs on the fully valid 01_ok_minimal.ucl aborts with `** (CaseClauseError) no case clause matching: %{zones: %{test: %{...}}, rooms: %{...}, room_exits: %{...}}`. The .exs therefore fails on 100% of inputs.
known_exs_defects_do_not_reproduce.python_must: return a verdict for every input, never crash
use [ \t] so consecutive `}`-only lines are legal

known_exs_defects_do_not_reproduce.defect: check_encoding/1 only rejects a FF FE prefix; it never checks the UTF-8 BOM.
